title: Focus. Desire.
editor: Doris Gassert, Stefan Gronert, Christopher A. Nixon, Sprengel Museum Hannover

description.main: Catalogue for Paul Mpagi Sepuya's exhibition at Fotomuseum Winterthur and the Sprengel Museum Hannover in 2026, his first solo show in the German-speaking world. 108 pages, 70 colour illustrations, Spector Books.
description.extended:
The catalogue for Focus. Desire., Paul Mpagi Sepuya's first solo exhibition in the German-speaking world, and the first book on him published there.

The show opened at Fotomuseum Winterthur in February 2026 and moved to the Sprengel Museum Hannover from July to October. Sepuya photographs friends and collaborators in his studio, often with himself and the camera in the frame. Mirrors, black drapes and props divide the picture, so that bodies appear reflected, cropped, doubled or partly hidden, and the act of taking the photograph becomes part of what is shown. The work insists on queer and Black subjects in photography. The book covers early and recent work, with material from the artist's archive and new essays. It was edited by Doris Gassert of Fotomuseum Winterthur, Stefan Gronert of the Sprengel Museum and the independent curator Christopher A. Nixon, and designed by Quang Nguyen of Good Enough, Berlin. It is a saddle-stitched softcover, 23 × 32 cm, with 108 pages and 70 colour illustrations, published in Leipzig by Spector Books with Fotomuseum Winterthur.

Sepuya was born in San Bernardino, California, in 1982 and lives in Los Angeles. The library also holds his Aperture monograph Paul Mpagi Sepuya (2022), Dark Room A–Z (2024), the zine D-R-M / P-X / B-F-D and Shoot (Primary Information, 2026).

notes: Exhibition: Fotomuseum Winterthur, February–June 2026; Sprengel Museum Hannover, July–October 2026 (dates per Twelvebooks). Spector lists publication as Leipzig, July 2026; AbeBooks lists April 2026. Editors per Spector: Doris Gassert, Stefan Gronert, Christopher A. Nixon, Sprengel Museum Hannover. Contents per Twelvebooks: early to recent works, material from the artist's personal archive, newly commissioned essays (essay authors not named on publisher page). Cover is Twelvebooks' 1700x1600 product shot cropped to the board; Spector's own cover image is 272x375.
